meta.title: Glossary of historical name forms
meta.note: Name forms only as given in the cited pages (read on the box copies: SFDAS_HCS2017 PDF, printed page = PDF page - 15; HD2011 intro, pp.1-7). Cite ids are registered in data/periods.json. term_ar only where a cited page prints the Arabic form (khartoum, port_sudan: QASIM_MAWSUA vol. 4, checked on page image), tagged [يحتاج تحقق] and queued; otherwise none supplied. Variant spellings in French follow SFDAS (e.g. Koush, Méroé, Fung, Bedjas).
meta.rendering: Web Lead renders; badges use the project badge set.

entries.note_en: Egyptian texts call Kerma 'Kush' from Senusret I (c.1950 BCE), and Greek sources from Herodotus on call the kingdom of Kush 'Ethiopia' (Aithiopia), a name later taken up for Abyssinia.
The northernmost of the three mid-6th-century Nubian kingdoms, bordering Egypt, with its capital at Qasr Ibrim and later Faras.
The central Nubian kingdom between the Third and Fifth Cataracts, with its capital at Old Dongola; a quoted medieval Arabic description calls it Muqurra.
The southernmost Nubian kingdom, above the Fifth Cataract to beyond modern Khartoum, with its capital at Soba on the Blue Nile.
SFDAS calls the Medjay ancestors of the Beja and the Blemmyes a Cushitic people related to the Beja, and says later written sources no longer distinguish Blemmyes from Beja.
entries.badge_note: Ancestry links across two millennia are an interpretation from one synthesis; no second source read.

entries.note_en: The Funj sultanate of Sennar was expanding into Nubia from the south when the Ottomans met it in battle at Hannek.
The Keira dynasty, from the Fur who give Darfur its name, replaced the Tunjur; SFDAS places this around the mid-16th century, earlier than the registry's 1650 start.
entries.badge_note: Founding date: SFDAS p.435 'vers le milieu du xvie siècle' vs era start 1650 in data/periods.json.

entries.note_en: A small Muslim kingdom in the north-eastern Nuba Mountains that kept semi-autonomy after the Turco-Egyptian conquest; its royal family traces its origin to a Ja'ali holy man.
entries.badge_note: REPORTED applies to the origin story only: oral tradition, per HD2011 p.4.

entries.note_en: The state founded by the Mahdi's movement; SFDAS dates the Mahdiyya 1885–1898 and Holt & Daly title the period 'The Mahdist State: 1881–98'.
The joint British-Egyptian regime over the territories south of Egypt, 1899–1955 per Holt & Daly, set up by Kitchener after Omdurman.
Medieval Muslim geographers' name for the belt of Africa south of the Sahara; Holt & Daly use 'eastern Bilad al-Sudan' for the lands south of Egypt.
Arabic form as printed in QASIM_MAWSUA vol. 4 ('جامعة الخرطوم', 'معهد الخرطوم الدولى').
Arabic form as printed in QASIM_MAWSUA vol. 4 ('معهد بورتسودان').
